content_html:
With tile floors, cleaning depends on both the tile and the grout. Ceramic and porcelain usually tolerate mild detergent, while natural stone and some sealers need pH-appropriate products.

Identify the material before using acid

Vinegar and acidic cleaners can etch marble, travertine, and other calcium-based stone. If you are unsure of the material, start with a neutral cleaner.

Dry-remove grit first

Sweeping or vacuuming keeps dirt from turning into mud and reduces wear on glazed surfaces and grout.

Mop with a low cleaner concentration

Too much detergent leaves a film and can make tile look dull. Follow the dose, replace dirty water, and dry the floor if streaks remain.

Grout may need separate attention

A nylon-bristle brush and compatible cleaner can work the grout without scratching tile. If grout is sealed, avoid products that degrade the sealer. For grout lines, use a separate soft brush and a cleaner compatible with both grout and tile. Avoid assuming that a product safe for ceramic tile is automatically suitable for natural stone or specialty grout.
